overall: Atlanta is tracking a warm early-June afternoon, with the running max sitting at 84.2°F as of 16:19 ET and temperatures still climbing at +1.7°F/hr — meaning the daily peak has not yet been reached. The high dewpoint of 66.2°F is adding humidity, making it feel muggy, while the 16.1 mph winds have not been enough to cap the warming. The temperature trajectory accelerated notably in the afternoon, jumping ~9°F between 13:00 and 16:15.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS and HRRR are in strong agreement at 85.4°F, while ECMWF and NBM are slightly more conservative at 83.8°F and 84.1°F respectively — a moderate spread of about 1.6°F across the four models. Observed temperatures are currently running slightly above ECMWF and NBM but have not yet reached the GFS/HRRR consensus, suggesting the observed max will likely settle somewhere in the middle of the model range.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 84.2°F, a still-positive warming rate of +1.7°F/hr at 16:19 ET, and GFS/HRRR both pegging the high at 85.4°F, additional warming of roughly 1-1.5°F before the evening cool-down seems probable.
